decisions: umbrella Amendment L, Ruling 1 and Ruling 3
umbrella Amendment M, Ruling 1 and Ruling 3
what_lands: The first of the fourteen. Amendment M, Ruling 1 orders delta_amp/receipt_walk to retire first and rules that its retirement act IS the walk-side delivery of the holder's static, pair-local amplifiers. So this slice lands the declared amp term on the from-declaration pricing stage Amendment L, Ruling 3 budgeted: a DeclaredPacket composed with the holder's static amps, resolved at build time from the declarations that produce them, and applied pre-mitigation so the composed value is mitigated once rather than a mitigated number being re-multiplied. The receipt walk gains its delta_amp interpreter, which is what a (family, RECEIPT_WALK) deferral row retires against, and the row leaves the frontier's deferral set with the compiled lane's row keeping -- and correcting -- the reason the two used to share.

landed_against.rule: R-17/R-32/D-97 -- no baseline moves inside any semantic commit of this slice. The code lands against the committed baselines plus this allowlist; a re-capture, if the measurement ever asks for one, is the integration agent's own commit.

qualifying_population.rule: R-20's second half. The count is not readable off the pre-change tree by inspection: this slice moves where a term comes from rather than editing a formula, so which leaves can move is a property of which participants have an amp armed, and that is a fact about the committed scenario set rather than about the diff. The population is therefore enumerated from committed artifacts -- scripts/golden_coupled_baseline.json's scenario subtrees, selected by golden_snapshot.holder_amp_declarations() joined against golden_snapshot.covering_scenarios() -- before the slice's first src/ edit. Any occurrence outside it is an unexpected one and stops the slice exactly as an over-count would.
qualifying_population.predicate: Every committed coupled scenario that arms at least one static holder amp, i.e. that puts a declaring owner of one of the three amp kinds on a participant. The three kinds and their owners are read live from the behaviour catalog over rule_owners() -- ability_part_amp/Actualizer, basic_part_amp/Hexoptics C44, magic_damage_amp/Abyssal Mask -- which is the same reading Amendment M, Ruling 2's coverage guard makes, so the population and the guard cannot disagree about which rosters can see the term. A scenario in which every amp reads 1.0 holds no leaf this slice can move, and the whole coupled snapshot outside these three subtrees is therefore outside the population.
qualifying_population.method: scripts.receipt_walk_schedule.population_size over each selected scenario subtree of the committed coupled baseline -- the same instrument, and the same conservative bound, the retirement schedule uses for the fourteen rows: the whole scenario subtree, because a slice that moves a family's pricing can move any aggregate downstream of it inside that scenario.

pair_engine_population.why: scripts/golden_baseline.json is the one-attacker pair-engine surface, and this slice adds no pair-engine arithmetic, authors no pair-engine breakdown row and stamps none: the amp term lands on the walk's own pricer. Zero pair-engine golden diffs is therefore a declared population of zero rather than an observation, and a single diff there stops the slice.

qualifying_population.predicted: 0 occurrences inside a population of 3015. The amp term is composed onto a DeclaredPacket, and no packet the tree produces carries a declaration -- tests/test_survival_kernel.py::TestThePathIsInertUntilAFamilyOptsIn asserts exactly that, by a scan over every src/calculator module, and this slice does not write the first construction. So the term is armed and reaches nothing, every roster total still holds the holder's amps exactly where it held them (folded into the pair engine's rows by damage._mitigate and damage._add_item_proc_damage), and the three amp-armed subtrees are unmoved. Zero is a legal and common R-20 value; stating it is what makes a first occurrence a stop.

why_no_pair_row_is_stamped.rule: Amendment L, Ruling 1 requires a retiring family's pair rows to be stamped pair_preview_of and declared THEORETICAL, and Amendment M, Ruling 1 narrows this family's retiring act to the static holder amps.
why_no_pair_row_is_stamped.measured: The three static holder amps author no pair-engine breakdown row. magic_amp is a factor inside damage._mitigate (damage.py:394-405), ability_amp multiplies the per-proc figure inside damage._add_item_proc_damage (damage.py:7509), and basic_amp multiplies inside damage._mitigate_basic_attack_swing (damage.py:637). Each folds into a row some other family owns; none is a row of its own. The two pair-lane rows the tree does stamp -- shadowflame_<owner> and expose_weakness_<owner> -- belong to mechanics already ruled and already stamped, and neither is a static holder amp.
why_no_pair_row_is_stamped.consequence: The set of pair-lane rows this family authors is empty, so the stamping half of Ruling 1 is discharged as an emptiness rather than performed. Stamping a row this family does not author would demote another family's number, which is the deletion Ruling 1's second forbidden shape names. Recorded here rather than left silent, because a discharged-as-empty clause and an unperformed one look identical from outside.
why_no_pair_row_is_stamped.what_keeps_it_honest: D-62's uniqueness property is asserted directly instead: no leaf sums a pair-authored preview and the walk's amp'd number. It holds vacuously today and is the invariant the next thirteen retirement slices land against, which is the reason to pin it on the commit that arms the term rather than on the commit that first pays one.

reason_text_correction.rule: R-36 -- the machine-derived frontier receipt moves with the slice that moves its count.
reason_text_correction.old_reason: neither walk reads an amp declaration: a holder-side amp reaches it already priced inside the pair engine's damage rows, and a cross-participant one as the damage_modifier packet item_support_effects emits, which survival/transitions stages as an ActionKind.DAMAGE_MODIFIER -- two routes, neither of them the rule
reason_text_correction.why_it_had_to_change: The two rows shared one reason object, and its first clause -- 'neither walk reads an amp declaration' -- stops being true of the receipt walk on the commit that registers its interpreter. A retired row that left its reason behind for the surviving row would leave the frontier stating, in the tree's own words, the opposite of what the tree does. The retirement schedule additionally records this reason as a prose/structure mismatch (a_second_and_smaller_mismatch): the row's structured via declares ['pair_engine'] while the prose names two routes and says neither is the rule, and Amendment K ruled that correcting it would be a behaviour claim owing its own slice rather than a schedule's edit. This is that slice.

no_baseline_moves: R-32's five baselines are untouched by every commit of this slice. docs/behavior-frontier.json and docs/receipts/receipt-walk-retirement-schedule.json are machine-derived receipts whose counters this slice moves, so they move with it (R-36); holding them back would make the slice red against a gate it is forbidden to contain.
